cohort: 16 women (8 vaginal delivery, 8 caesarean delivery) at six-weeks postpartum
finding: Breastmilk at six-weeks postpartum had a low microbial load, and the identified microbes were mostly consistent with skin and oral microbes, suggesting that breastmilk at this stage does not have a distinct microbiota.
mod_finding: The study included women who delivered by vaginal (n=8) and caesarean delivery (n=8) but did not find an association between mode of delivery and the breastmilk microbiota at six-weeks postpartum.
